name: Bay of Islands
tagline: A beautiful, history-laden stretch of coast where New Zealand's founding document was signed, 144 islands scatter across sheltered water, and sailing is simply the way of life.
highlight: Cruising out through the Hole in the Rock, a natural arch worn clean through Motukokako Island by the sea.
shortDescription: A sheltered coastline of 144 islands in New Zealand's far north, central to the country's history and its sailing culture alike.
metaDescription: A Bay of Islands travel guide: Waitangi, Russell, the Hole in the Rock, when to go and how to plan a relaxed few days by the water.
nearestAirport: Bay of Islands Airport (Kerikeri, KKE), or Auckland Airport (AKL)
knownFor: Waitangi Treaty Grounds, sailing, the Hole in the Rock, Russell
goodFor: New Zealand history, sailing and boat cruises, a slower coastal pace

image.file: File:Motukokako Island (Piercy Island) with Hole in the Rock.jpg
image.alt: The Hole in the Rock, a natural arch through Motukokako Island in the Bay of Islands

intro: The Bay of Islands is where modern New Zealand began — the Treaty of Waitangi, the country's founding document, was signed here in 1840 on the lawn in front of the Treaty House, and the bay's early role as a whaling and trading port shaped the nation long before Auckland or Wellington existed.

That history sits alongside 144 islands scattered across sheltered, island-studded water, drawing sailors, game fishers and cruise passengers to a coastline that has quietly functioned as New Zealand's boating playground for well over a century.
It's a slower, warmer corner of the country than the South Island's mountain scenery — the appeal here is history, water and a relaxed subtropical pace rather than dramatic landscapes.

whyVisit.intro: The Bay of Islands' case rests on a rare combination of national history and a beautiful, boat-friendly coastline.

points.title: Waitangi is New Zealand's most significant historic site
points.text: The country's founding treaty between the British Crown and Maori chiefs was signed on these grounds in 1840.

points.title: The Hole in the Rock is one of the North Island's most photographed sights
points.text: A natural arch worn clean through solid rock, reachable by scenic cruise from Paihia or Russell.

points.title: Russell is New Zealand's first capital and a beautifully preserved colonial township
points.text: Once a rough whaling port nicknamed the 'hellhole of the Pacific,' now a quiet, historic seaside village.

points.title: The sailing culture is woven into daily life here, not a tourist add-on
points.text: The bay has hosted serious yachting and game fishing for well over a century.

points.title: It's a warmer, more relaxed pace than much of the rest of the country
points.text: Northland's subtropical climate makes the Bay of Islands pleasant to visit across most of the year.

attractionsIntro: The Bay of Islands' essential sights span its founding history, its historic townships, and its scattered islands offshore.

attractions.name: Waitangi Treaty Grounds

image.file: File:00 27 0577 Waitangi, New Zealand - Treaty House.jpg
image.alt: The Treaty House at the Waitangi Treaty Grounds

attractions.text: The genuine birthplace of modern New Zealand, where the Treaty of Waitangi was signed in 1840, with the Treaty House, a carved meeting house and the world's largest ceremonial war canoe on site.
attractions.tip: A guided tour adds far more historical context than walking the grounds alone.

attractions.name: Russell

image.file: File:00 26 0874 Russell Neuseeland - Bay of Islands.jpg
image.alt: The historic waterfront township of Russell in the Bay of Islands

attractions.text: New Zealand's first capital and a rowdy 19th-century whaling port, now a beautifully preserved, quiet township reached by a short ferry from Paihia.
attractions.tip: Climb Maiki (Flagstaff) Hill for an excellent view over the whole bay.

attractions.name: The Hole in the Rock

image.file: File:Motukokako Island (Piercy Island) with Hole in the Rock.jpg
image.alt: The Hole in the Rock, a natural arch through Motukokako Island

attractions.text: A striking natural arch worn through Motukokako Island by wind and sea, with calm-weather cruises passing directly through it.
attractions.tip: Passage through the hole depends on swell conditions — it isn't guaranteed on every cruise.

attractions.name: Kerikeri's Stone Store and Kemp House

image.alt: The historic Stone Store in Kerikeri, New Zealand's oldest stone building

attractions.text: New Zealand's oldest stone building and oldest wooden building sit side by side here, remnants of one of the country's earliest mission stations.
attractions.tip: The Kerikeri Basin walk links the historic buildings to a waterfall a short stroll away.

attractions.name: Cape Brett Track and Lighthouse

image.file: File:Lighthouse and Cape Brett Hut (former lighthouse keeper's house).jpg
image.alt: The lighthouse and former keeper's house at Cape Brett

attractions.text: A demanding full-day or overnight track to a working lighthouse at the bay's outermost point, with dramatic coastal views throughout.
attractions.tip: Most visitors see the cape by boat instead — the track is a serious hike, not a casual walk.

attractions.name: Paihia

image.alt: The waterfront at Paihia, the main town of the Bay of Islands

attractions.text: The bay's genuine hub town, its waterfront lined with cruise operators, cafés and the short ferry crossing to Russell.
attractions.tip: Most cruises and activities depart directly from the Paihia wharf.

attractions.name: The bay's 144 islands

image.file: File:Hat Island (Left, in distance) Mahenotiti Island (Centre) and Te Ao Island (Right) as viewed from Urupukapuka..jpg
image.alt: Islands scattered across the Bay of Islands, viewed from Urupukapuka Island

attractions.text: A vast, sheltered scattering of islands and inlets, with Urupukapuka the largest, offering beaches and walking tracks reached only by boat.
attractions.tip: A full-day cruise covers far more of the bay than a short harbour trip.

thingsToDoIntro: The Bay of Islands centres on the water, with history-rich towns to explore between cruises.

thingsToDo.title: Cruise to the Hole in the Rock

image.file: File:Motukokako Island (Piercy Island) with Hole in the Rock.jpg
image.alt: A cruise boat approaching the Hole in the Rock

thingsToDo.text: The essential Bay of Islands excursion, a half-day cruise out to Cape Brett and, conditions allowing, straight through the rock arch.
thingsToDo.tip: Sit outside on the upper deck for the best photos as the boat passes through.

thingsToDo.title: Sail the Bay of Islands

image.alt: Sailboats on the water in the Bay of Islands

thingsToDo.text: A serious sailing destination for well over a century, with day charters and multi-day yacht trips widely available from Paihia and Opua.
thingsToDo.tip: A skippered half-day sail needs no prior sailing experience.

thingsToDo.title: Swim or cruise with dolphins
thingsToDo.text: Common dolphins are frequent visitors to the bay, with dedicated dolphin-watching and swim tours running from Paihia.
thingsToDo.tip: Swimming is weather- and dolphin-behaviour-dependent, so treat it as a bonus rather than a guarantee.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the Cape Brett Track

image.file: File:Lighthouse and Cape Brett Hut (former lighthouse keeper's house).jpg
image.alt: The Cape Brett lighthouse at the end of the Cape Brett Track

thingsToDo.text: A serious 16km one-way tramp to the lighthouse, usually done as an overnight trip with a stay in the DOC hut.
thingsToDo.tip: This is a strenuous full-day hike each way — fit trampers only.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Waitangi Treaty Grounds

image.file: File:00 27 0577 Waitangi, New Zealand - Treaty House.jpg
image.alt: Visitors at the Waitangi Treaty Grounds

thingsToDo.text: An essential few hours spent on the site where New Zealand's founding document was signed, including a Maori cultural performance.
thingsToDo.tip: Time your visit around one of the scheduled cultural performances for the fullest experience.

thingsToDo.title: Wander historic Russell

image.file: File:00 26 0874 Russell Neuseeland - Bay of Islands.jpg
image.alt: Wandering the historic waterfront of Russell

thingsToDo.text: An easy, pleasant afternoon spent among New Zealand's oldest church, its first capital's colonial buildings, and a quiet waterfront.
thingsToDo.tip: The passenger ferry from Paihia runs regularly throughout the day.

foodIntro: The Bay of Islands' food leans on fresh local seafood, alongside the standard New Zealand classics found countrywide.

foods.name: Green-lipped mussels

image.alt: A plate of New Zealand green-lipped mussels

foods.text: A distinctive native species, farmed in sheltered northern waters and served simply steamed at waterfront restaurants.
foods.whereToTry: Waterfront restaurants in Paihia and Russell.

foods.name: Fish and chips

image.alt: A classic New Zealand fish and chips takeaway

foods.text: Best eaten on the Paihia waterfront, fresh off the day's catch and eaten looking out over the bay.
foods.whereToTry: Waterfront takeaways in Paihia and Russell.

foods.name: Pavlova

image.alt: A pavlova dessert topped with cream and fresh fruit

foods.text: A beloved national dessert, its crisp meringue shell and soft centre a fixture on café menus across the bay.

foods.name: Kumara
foods.text: An important Maori and New Zealand staple, this native sweet potato appears roasted, mashed or as chips on menus throughout Northland.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants throughout Paihia, Russell and Kerikeri.

foods.name: Manuka honey

image.alt: Jars of New Zealand manuka honey

foods.text: Northland's warm climate makes it prime manuka country, and local honey is sold direct from producers around Kerikeri.
foods.whereToTry: Farm shops and gift stores around Kerikeri.

foods.name: Flat white

image.file: File:Flat white coffee Highgate Cricket Club, Crouch End, London 01.jpg
image.alt: A flat white coffee, a New Zealand café staple

foods.text: Essential before a day out on the water, and Paihia's waterfront cafés keep a steady, reliable standard.

accommodation.intro: Paihia is the most convenient base, with Russell offering a quieter, more historic alternative just a ferry ride away.

areas.name: Paihia
areas.bestFor: Cruise departures and the widest choice of accommodation
areas.text: The bay's genuine hub, with most tour operators and restaurants within walking distance of the waterfront.

areas.name: Russell
areas.text: Charming and peaceful, a short ferry ride from Paihia's activity and restaurant scene.

areas.name: Kerikeri
areas.bestFor: A more local, less touristy base
areas.text: A pleasant small town a short drive inland, handy for the historic Stone Store precinct.

gettingThere.intro: The Bay of Islands sits a comfortable drive north of Auckland, with a small local airport for quicker access.

options.text: About 3h15 drive from [[auckland|Auckland]], straightforward on the main state highway north.
options.detail: A worthwhile stop is Whangarei's Town Basin, roughly the halfway point.

options.text: Short flights connect Auckland to the Bay of Islands Airport at Kerikeri.
options.detail: A quick option if you'd rather skip the drive.

options.text: InterCity coaches run from Auckland to Paihia.
options.detail: A workable, if slower, budget option for visitors without a car.

gettingAround.intro: Paihia and Russell are linked by a short, frequent passenger ferry, while a car helps reach Kerikeri and the wider region.

options.text: A quick, frequent crossing running throughout the day.
options.detail: Far simpler than driving around the harbour to reach Russell.

options.text: Useful for reaching Kerikeri and Northland's wider sights independently.
options.detail: Most key towns sit within a 30-minute drive of each other.

options.text: Widely available from Paihia for the Hole in the Rock, dolphin watching and Cape Brett.
options.detail: The standard way most visitors see the bay's outer islands.

bestTime.headline: Spring through autumn, with a warm, mild climate for most of the year
bestTime.summary: Northland's subtropical climate keeps the Bay of Islands pleasant across a wider window than much of the rest of the country.

seasons.text: Warm, busy and the peak season for sailing and cruises.
Settled and warm, with noticeably thinner crowds than summer.
Mild by New Zealand standards, though wetter, with quieter towns and lower prices.
Increasingly warm and pleasant, ahead of the summer peak.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — Northland's climate stays mild year-round, though summer weekends and school holidays bring the biggest crowds.

tipsIntro: Practical notes on booking, ferries and timing that make a real difference to a Bay of Islands trip.
tips: Book Hole in the Rock cruises ahead in summer — the best morning departures fill up.
Check whether your cruise actually passes through the arch — it's subject to swell conditions.
Catch the passenger ferry rather than driving to Russell — it's quicker and removes parking hassle.
Bring sun protection even on overcast days — Northland's subtropical sun is stronger than further south.
Book Cape Brett Hut well ahead if attempting the full track — it's popular in summer.
Combine the Bay of Islands with Auckland on a northern road trip rather than treating it as an isolated stop.

faq.q: How many days do you need in the Bay of Islands?
faq.a: Three days covers Waitangi, a Hole in the Rock cruise and Russell comfortably. A day trip from Auckland is possible but rushed.

faq.q: Is the Bay of Islands worth visiting for history?
faq.a: Yes — Waitangi is New Zealand's single most significant historic site, and Russell was the country's first capital.

faq.q: Does the cruise always go through the Hole in the Rock?
faq.a: Not guaranteed — passage depends on swell and tide conditions on the day, though most cruises attempt it.

faq.q: Is Russell or Paihia the better base?
faq.a: Paihia is more convenient for cruises and restaurants; Russell offers a quieter, more historic stay a short ferry ride away.

faq.q: Can you swim with dolphins in the Bay of Islands?
faq.a: Yes, on dedicated tours, though it's dependent on finding dolphins and their behaviour on the day — treat it as a possibility, not a guarantee.

faq.q: Do you need a car in the Bay of Islands?
faq.a: It helps for reaching Kerikeri and wider Northland, though Paihia and Russell themselves are easily covered on foot and by ferry.
